standard.title: Share a perspective
standard.description: share a perspective on information, such as stories about significant events and special places
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have opinions and preferences from lived experience. No formal prior HASS inquiry skills curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share their own perspective on information about significant events and special places, using sources to support their view.

nodes.label: Recognising that perspectives differ
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise that different people can have different views about the same event or place, and that both can be valid.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify that two people in a story or class discussion have different views about the same thing and describe what each person thinks.
nodes.typical_width: Explore provided stories or class discussions where perspectives differ; identify what shapes each perspective (personal experience, cultural background, what someone values).
wider: Compare how the same celebration or place is viewed differently by different family members or cultural groups
Explore First Nations Australian perspectives on places that are also significant to other community members
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot recognise that perspectives differ will present their own view as universal fact, making it impossible for them to genuinely share a perspective (as distinct from stating a fact) in Node 2.

response_modes.reason: Perspective-taking is conceptually demanding at Foundation — use concrete scenarios where the divergence is clear and meaningful before asking students to apply the concept to their own views.

success_criteria: Identifies that at least two people have different views about the same event or place
Describes what each person thinks without judging one as wrong

nodes.label: Sharing my own perspective
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share their own perspective on a significant event or special place, explaining why they feel that way and using a source to support their view.
nodes.minimum_width: Share a personal view about a special place or significant event and give one reason for that view.
nodes.typical_width: Share perspectives on stories about significant events and special places using provided sources; explain why the place or event is important from their own point of view; connect their perspective to personal experience.
wider: Share perspectives about a place that is important to past generations of their family, explaining why those events and places are special
Listen to a First Nations Australian story about a special place and share a response, comparing it with their own experience of special places

response_modes.reason: A range of significant events and places gives students more contexts to form and share views — class diversity is the primary resource here.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The class's diversity of backgrounds means that perspectives on celebrations, places and events will genuinely differ, creating authentic contexts for perspective-sharing and respectful listening.
success_criteria: Shares a personal view about a significant event or special place
Gives at least one reason for that view
